title: Phase Sensitivity of Spectrally Multimode SU(1,1) Interferometers with Waveguide based Optical Parametric Amplifier
authors: Sonu Jana, Swagatam Bag, Fabien Bretenaker, Nadia Belabas, Syamsundar De
abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for evaluating the phase sensitivity of spectrally multimode SU(1,1) interferometers probed with a coherent-vacuum input, under both number and homodyne detections. The optical parametric amplifiers (OPAs) are simulated using a periodically polled thin-film lithium niobate waveguide. The theoretical model incorporates the intrinsic multimode spectral nature of waveguide-based OPAs. Under the assumptions of identical OPAs and Schmidt-mode-independent phase shifts, we have shown that the multimode SU(1,1) interferometer is equivalent to a collection of independent single-mode interferometers in the Schmidt basis that operate in parallel, each associated with a Schmidt mode of the parametric process. We further present an optimized waveguide design based on asymmetric group-velocity matching to realize a practical OPA with nearly factorizable joint spectral amplitude (JSA). The Schmidt coefficients extracted from the numerically simulated JSA are incorporated into the theoretical model to evaluate the phase sensitivity. The results show that the sensitivity under a multimode condition depends strongly on the measurement scheme. For number detection, the degradation in sensitivity arises from the redistribution of the available nonlinear resource among the Schmidt modes, whereas homodyne detection exhibits an additional coherence penalty that can be substantially reduced by optimally shaping the local oscillator. Moreover, we show that the performance degradation can be to a large extent mitigated by optimizing the spectrum of the injected signal coherent state and, in the case of homodyne detection, the spectrum of the local oscillator. Altogether, this work provides a unified theoretical and numerical framework for analyzing and optimizing realistic multimode SU(1,1) interferometers with waveguide-based OPAs for quantum-enhanced sensing applications.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive framework to assess the phase sensitivity of multimode $	ext{SU}(1,1)$ interferometers built using waveguide-based OPAs. By analyzing the system in the Schmidt basis, the authors show that while multi-mode operation introduces spectral penalties, these can be substantially reduced by optimizing both the input signal and the local oscillator spectrum, particularly when using homodyne detection.
main_problem: The study evaluates how the intrinsic spectral multimode nature of waveguide-based Optical Parametric Amplifiers (OPAs) affects the phase sensitivity achievable in an $	ext{SU}(1,1)$ interferometer.
main_result: Phase sensitivity depends strongly on the measurement scheme; while number detection suffers from resource redistribution penalties, homodyne detection allows for significant mitigation of degradation by optimizing the local oscillator spectrum and input signal state.
method: The analysis employs a theoretical framework utilizing the Schmidt basis decomposition of the Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA) to model the multimode evolution as a parallel collection of independent single-mode interferometers.
model_or_system: The system is an $	ext{SU}(1,1)$ interferometer realized using periodically polled thin-film lithium niobate ($	ext{PP-TFLN}$) waveguides acting as OPAs. The model incorporates the full multimode spectral structure derived from the PDC process.
key_observables: Phase sensitivity ($\Delta\varphi$); Sensitivity degradation penalty ratio ($\eta(r)$); Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA) and its Schmidt coefficients.
important_parameters: Detection scheme (number vs. homodyne); Input signal coherent state spectrum; Local oscillator spectrum; Total squeezing strength ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes identical OPAs and mode-independent phase shifts for simplification in the Schmidt basis representation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the interferometer, show how matching the probe spectrum to the dominant Schmidt mode mitigates degradation, and compare sensitivity ratios ($\eta(r)$) under different resource constraints.
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework by mapping the multimode $	ext{SU}(1,1)$ evolution onto independent single-mode transformations in the Schmidt basis. It then calculates phase sensitivity using error propagation for both number and homodyne detection, culminating in optimization strategies for input/LO spectra.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool to analyze quantum sensing limits in realistic, spectrally complex photonic platforms like integrated waveguides, bridging fundamental quantum optics theory with practical device engineering.
